$comment: How each published [ALLOWLIST-n] id is asserted. Checked by scripts/allowlist-coverage.mjs,
which runs the suites with a witness sink and compares what this file CLAIMS against what
actually executed.
This file declares intent. It is not evidence, and it cannot become evidence: an id declared
`policy` or `witness` here must produce witnesses at run time, from the declared MECHANISM,
covering the declared SUBJECTS, or the coverage check fails. That asymmetry is the point of
ISS-020 — the previous arrangement argued coverage from prose and from test NAMES, the same
'code exists, therefore it ran' reasoning that dual_run_only was removed to escape.
Modes (exactly these three; an unrecognized mode is an error, not a default):
policy   — consumed by a comparison policy in tests-ts/harness/policies.mjs. Witnessed by
tests-ts/parity.mjs with source 'policy', once per case, and only when the
policy actually performed at least one assertion. The subjects must equal the
case list ALLOWLIST.md publishes for the id.
witness  — asserted by a test that is NOT a parity case, which calls witness() itself with
source 'test'. `requiredSubjects` lists every assertion site that must fire;
exact agreement is required, so deleting one of several sites fails even though
the others still witness the id.
none     — deliberately not machine-asserted. Requires `why`. An id here that DOES emit a
witness is also a failure, because the declaration has gone stale in the
direction that understates what the tests do.

ALLOWLIST-14.why: Schema violations fail loud; asserted on argv_blocks_array.

ALLOWLIST-19.why: hourly --date values fromisoformat rejects; asserted on 13 cases.

why: The product-name spans in --help. There is no parity case: the approved artifact is the
shipped-help snapshot, so the assertion reads the snapshot rather than comparing two
implementations. This was the entry ISS-020 was filed about — it used to be documented
as 'snapshot-asserted, not machine-verified'. It is now machine-verified, by execution.
TWO sites are required, not one. The entry covers both that every command row names the
shipped program and that the oracle's program name appears nowhere as a command; those
are different claims, and requiring only 'some witness for 22a' would let either be
deleted while the other kept the entry looking covered.

ALLOWLIST-22b.why: The config-path sentence; the one sanctioned rewrite, then equality for the rest.

ALLOWLIST-23.why: A mid-render failure produces no partial stdout; asserted on two cases.

ALLOWLIST-25.why: Spawn-failure advice names CCUSAGE_CMD instead of npx; asserted on err_missing_binary.
